Bimuelos

Served at: Hanukkah (Festival of Lights)

Serves 6-8Prep 15 minCook 15 min

Bimuelos are traditional Sephardic Jewish fried dough balls enjoyed during Hanukkah, the Festival of Lights. They are sweet, fluffy, and often soaked in syrup or honey, symbolizing the miracle of the oil that lasted eight days. These treats bring warmth and joy to Hanukkah celebrations.

Ingredients

  • 2 cups all-purpose flour (240 g)
  • 1 tablespoon sugar
  • 1 teaspoon active dry yeast
  • 1/2 teaspoon salt
  • 3/4 cup warm water (180 ml)
  • 1 large egg
  • 1 teaspoon vanilla extract
  • Vegetable oil for frying
  • Honey or simple syrup for soaking

Method

  1. In a small bowl, dissolve the yeast and sugar in warm water; let sit for 5-10 minutes until frothy.
  2. In a large mixing bowl, combine the flour and salt.
  3. Add the yeast mixture, egg, and vanilla extract to the flour mixture; stir until a sticky dough forms.
  4. Cover the bowl with a clean towel and let the dough rise in a warm place for about 1 hour, or until doubled in size.
  5. Heat about 2 inches of vegetable oil in a deep pan to 350°F (175°C).
  6. Using a spoon or your hands, drop small portions of dough into the hot oil, frying a few at a time to avoid overcrowding.
  7. Fry the bimuelos for about 2-3 minutes per side, until golden brown and puffed up.
  8. Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels.
  9. While still warm, soak the bimuelos in honey or simple syrup for a few minutes before serving.

Tips

  • Ensure the oil temperature is steady at 350°F (175°C) for even frying and to avoid greasy bimuelos.
  • For a citrus twist, add a teaspoon of orange zest to the dough.
  • Serve with a dusting of powdered sugar or a drizzle of cinnamon sugar for extra flavor.
